reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it directly instructs viewers to register for Forsage, fund a Trust Wallet account, and join through a team or referral link. The supplied frames present Forsage as a matrix platform requiring an ETH payment and advertise a "Zero Risk Factors" assurance, while the speaker repeatedly directs viewers to register under a good team. These combined recruitment-dependent participation instructions and risk-free framing support a scam classification rather than an ordinary wallet tutorial.

opening.argument: Judge, the clearest caution in this walkthrough concerns wallet security. The setup instructions tell viewers not to share their twelve recovery words and identify them as private wallet information. The speaker also stops short of completing a registration on camera, saying they are already a member. That does not make the service safe, but it matters when assessing what this video itself establishes: it includes a concrete safeguard rather than asking viewers to disclose the credential that controls their wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to funding and a team link, but those facts do not erase the explicit instruction to keep recovery words private. The page's "Zero Risk Factors" language is a claim shown on the destination page; the speaker does not repeat it as a personal guarantee. The record supports concern about the service, but a displayed claim is not, by itself, proof that this speaker promises viewers a risk-free outcome.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning about protecting recovery words addresses credential theft, not the risk of paying to join Forsage. The instructions still direct viewers to fund a wallet with ETH and complete registration, while the description invites them to join through a team link. Stopping the demonstration because the speaker is already a member does not undo that invitation.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker introduces the video as instruction in setting up Trust Wallet and registering for Forsage. Much of the visible sequence follows that practical sequence: wallet setup, locating a receive address, and opening the destination page. The speaker explains how to copy an address so someone can fund the account, then says the demonstration cannot go further because they are already a member. Read as a whole, this is an operational walkthrough; explaining a process is not the same thing as substantiating an earnings promise.

opening.argument: Judge, the strongest inference supported by the spoken invitation is that the viewer can use a team link to register. The speaker tells viewers to copy a user ID and follow the site's joining steps, but does not state a commission rate, describe downline payouts, or promise returns. Even the displayed registration instructions describe a payment to join, not what any participant will earn from recruiting another person. A referral-linked sign-up may warrant scrutiny, but the record does not demonstrate the compensation mechanism that would distinguish it from an ordinary referral promotion.
